sentences.text:
I.A. No. 5272 of 2024 in Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 1507 of 2023 & I.A. No. 4469 of 2024 in Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 1885 of 2023 These interlocutory applications have been filed by the appellants, praying therein to suspend the sentence and release them on bail during the pendency of this appeal.
2. The appellants have been convicted under Sections 366, 376DA, 376(3), 511, 34 of IPC and Sections 6 and 18 of the POCSO Act in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 40 of 2019 arising out of Goilkera P.S. Case No. 20 of 2019.
They have been sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for twenty four years and a fine of Rs. 10,000/- each for the offence under Section 6 of POCSO Act.

3. Heard, the learned counsel for the appellants and learned A.P.P. for the State and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.

sentences.text: From the evidence of both the victims, it is evident that none of the victims has stated that they were sexually assaulted.
6. Considering the statement of the victims and the fact that there is no likelihood of hearing of this appeal in near future, we are inclined to allow these interlocutory applications.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellants, named above, are directed to be released on bail during the pendency of these appeals, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand only) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Addl. Sessions Judge-I-cum-Special Judge (POCSO) Act, West Singhbhum at Chaibasa, in connection with in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 40 of 2019 arising out of Goilkera P.S. Case No. 20 of 2019 with a condition that the appellants shall appear and mark their attendance before the Registrar,
Civil Court, West Singhbum, Chaibasa once in every four months till the disposal of these appeals.
